examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Marketing Cloud Engagement Administrator exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam covers account setup, security, subscriber data, and email deliverability. Prepare for Business Unit design, role-based access, and sender authentication settings.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
67% to pass, which is 41 correct answers out of 60.
Account administration. Study Business Units, IP warming, sender authentication, and API security.
Deliverability knowledge. Review SPF, DKIM, DMARC, Reply Mail Management, and IP reputation.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Hands-on account administration helps. Practise Business Unit setup, role assignment, sender authentication, and deliverability monitoring in a sandbox before booking.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Engagement Administrator exam format
examFormat.intro: The proctored exam is available online or at a test centre. Many questions describe an administrative task or incident.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios may ask how to configure access in a multi-Business Unit account, diagnose delivery issues, or set data retention rules.
bestWayToPass: Design Business Units: Understand parent and child settings, permission scope, and shared versus local data extensions.
Study sender reputation: Review IP warming, sender authentication, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and Reply Mail Management.
Manage users securely: Learn standard and custom roles, SSO, and IP allowlisting.
Review Marketing Cloud Connect: Understand the integration user, synchronized data, and sync troubleshooting.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers administration of Marketing Cloud Engagement, including Business Units, user permissions, subscriber data, sender authentication, deliverability, data retention, and Salesforce integration. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 67% pass mark, weighted towards Setup (38%) and Subscriber Data Management (18%).

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Engagement Administrator: topics to review

blocks.heading: Account structure and Business Units
blocks.body: Business Units separate users, subscriber data, sending configuration, and reporting, which can help organize brands or regions. The parent unit can manage shared assets and account-wide settings. Roles determine what users may do in a unit. A Sender Authentication Package can provide branded sending and tracking domains and a dedicated IP. Understand when a separate unit is needed and how permissions and shared data work across units.

blocks.heading: Subscriber records and preferences
blocks.body: All Subscribers is the account-level record of subscriber status; a global unsubscribe applies broadly. Publication lists let subscribers manage preferences by content type. Suppression lists exclude addresses from selected sends, while auto-suppression lists can apply across sends. Data extensions store structured subscriber or event data. Subscriber Key strategy, such as using a CRM ID rather than email, affects deduplication and cross-channel identity. Configure data models and retention according to business and privacy needs.

blocks.heading: IP warming and sender reputation
blocks.body: A new dedicated IP needs a gradual warming schedule, increasing volume over time to establish reputation with mailbox providers. Begin with engaged subscribers and monitor bounces, complaints, and inbox placement. Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC with the sender domain. Reply Mail Management can handle replies such as out-of-office messages and unsubscribe requests. Learn which metrics signal reputation problems.

blocks.heading: Roles, permissions, and account security
blocks.body: Access is controlled through roles and permissions at the Business Unit level. Users may have different roles in different units. SSO can connect Marketing Cloud to a corporate identity provider using supported protocols. IP allowlisting restricts where users can sign in; account security can also include multi-factor authentication. Data permissions control access to data extensions. Monitor logins and use installed packages for API integrations.

blocks.heading: Salesforce CRM integration
blocks.body: Marketing Cloud Connect links Engagement with Sales or Service Cloud. Synchronized data extensions can bring Leads, Contacts, Campaigns, and other CRM records into Marketing Cloud. Triggered sends can respond to Salesforce record changes. Journeys may use CRM data or synchronized data extensions as entry sources. Send results can be written back to Salesforce records. Administrators configure connections and sync schedules and troubleshoot synchronization errors.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Marketing Cloud Engagement Administrator exam
scenarioTips.intro: Practise how to configure, secure, and maintain a Marketing Cloud account, including users, data, delivery, and integration.

blocks.heading: Configure account structure
blocks.body: Plan Business Units for brands or regions, understand inherited permissions, and manage shared assets and data extensions.

blocks.heading: Assign least-privilege roles
blocks.body: Review standard roles, custom roles, and which studio or account features each role can access.

blocks.heading: Manage data and retention
blocks.body: Configure data extension retention, maintain subscriber status, and learn Contact Deletion for privacy requests.

blocks.heading: Configure sender authentication
blocks.body: Understand the domains, IP options, and Reply Mail Management included with a Sender Authentication Package and how it differs from shared sending.

blocks.heading: Secure API integrations
blocks.body: Create installed packages with OAuth credentials, restrict IP access where appropriate, and monitor API activity.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketing user needs to create and send email but must not change account settings. What access should the admin assign?
options: A role with content and send permissions only
The Administrator role for the user’s Business Unit
A new Business Unit with the user as administrator
A shared administrator login
sampleQuestions.explanation: A role limited to content and sending lets the user do the job without account-level administration.
whyWrong: Administrator access includes the settings that should remain restricted.
Creating another unit and giving administrator access still grants excessive rights.
Shared accounts remove user-level accountability.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Sender Authentication Package typically provide?
options: A collection of email templates for each studio
Prebuilt journeys ready to activate
A branded sending domain and dedicated IP
A weekly deliverability report
sampleQuestions.explanation: The package can provide branded sending and tracking domains and a dedicated IP for sending reputation.
whyWrong: Templates are created in Content Builder.
Journeys are configured for the customer’s use case.
Reporting is separate from sender authentication.

sampleQuestions.question: A large data extension query is slow. What should the admin check first?
options: Move the extension to a new Business Unit
Add a primary key and index the fields used in filters
Rebuild it as an All Subscribers list
Split it into twelve monthly extensions immediately
sampleQuestions.explanation: Keys and indexes can help the platform locate rows without scanning the entire table.
whyWrong: Business Units organize access but do not directly improve query performance.
Subscriber lists are not a replacement for a structured data extension.
Splitting creates extra complexity and may require combining results.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a data extension retention policy do?
options: Prevents users from deleting rows manually
Copies records to an archive extension before deletion
Compresses old rows to save space
Deletes rows or the extension after the configured period
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retention settings remove data after the defined period, either by row or for the entire extension.
whyWrong: Retention does not prevent a user with permission from deleting data.
An archive copy is not automatically created by the policy.
Retention deletes data; it is not a compression feature.

sampleQuestions.question: A partner should access data for one brand only. What is the best structure?
options: Create additional roles in the existing Business Unit only
Purchase a separate Marketing Cloud contract for the partner
Share one account login and explain which folders to use
Create a Business Unit for the brand and scope partner users to it
sampleQuestions.explanation: Business Units help separate brand data and access. Limit the partner’s users to the relevant unit.
whyWrong: Roles control actions but do not by themselves isolate brand data.
A separate contract may be unnecessary when a Business Unit meets the access need.
Instructions are not a security control.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a send classification define?
options: The sender profile and delivery profile for a send
The order of automation activities
Which content blocks appear in an email
The maximum number of subscribers per send
sampleQuestions.explanation: A send classification associates sender and delivery profiles and identifies the send type.
whyWrong: Automation order is set in the workflow.
Email content is configured in the message.
Audience limits are not set by the classification.

sampleQuestions.question: A nightly import fails without notice. What should the admin configure?
options: A longer file transfer window regardless of the cause
Error notifications for the automation
A duplicate automation that runs later
A daily manual check by the marketing team
sampleQuestions.explanation: Automation notifications can alert the team when an activity fails.
whyWrong: A longer window helps only if the failure is caused by a timeout.
A duplicate can repeat the failure and create other issues.
A manual daily check is slower and less reliable than an alert.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the All Subscribers list?
options: A Content Builder folder of journey audiences
The account-level record of subscriber identities and status
A report of the latest email openers
A list that admins rebuild before each major send
sampleQuestions.explanation: All Subscribers maintains account-level subscriber records and global unsubscribe status.
whyWrong: It stores subscriber records rather than content assets.
It is not an engagement report.
The platform maintains it; administrators do not rebuild it for each send.

sampleQuestions.question: How can an administrator move supported assets between Marketing Cloud Business Units?
options: Export and import every item manually
Rebuild all assets in the production unit
Use Package Manager to package and deploy assets
Ask Salesforce Support to copy the account configuration
sampleQuestions.explanation: Package Manager can bundle and deploy supported assets between units.
whyWrong: Manual transfer is slower and can break asset relationships.
Rebuilding introduces avoidable differences.
Routine asset migration is handled with platform tools.

sampleQuestions.question: What happens when an address is added to a global suppression list?
options: It is excluded from sends across the account
It can receive transactional sends but not commercial sends
It moves automatically to a holding Business Unit
Its subscriber record is deleted from every data extension
sampleQuestions.explanation: Global suppression excludes the address from sends across the account.
whyWrong: Global suppression is broader than a commercial-only restriction.
Suppression does not move the contact to another unit.
Suppression excludes an address; it does not delete stored data.

sampleQuestions.question: A subscriber receives the same email twice. What is one likely cause?
options: The journey was activated twice by two users
The email contains duplicate content blocks
The person exists under different Subscriber Keys
The send classification is transactional
sampleQuestions.explanation: Different Subscriber Keys can represent the same person as separate records and lead to duplicate sends.
whyWrong: Activating a journey creates versions, not necessarily duplicate messages.
Repeated content affects layout, not the number of sends.
Send classification does not create duplicate subscribers.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool can show account logins and configuration changes?
options: A weekly deliverability report
A query against subscriber data views
Audit Trail
The tracking report for each email job
sampleQuestions.explanation: Audit Trail records security and configuration events such as logins and setting changes.
whyWrong: Deliverability reports cover sending performance.
Data views cover send and engagement data rather than administration events.
Email tracking reports describe message results.

sampleQuestions.question: What does marking a data extension as sendable allow?
options: Automatic nightly backup
Exemption from retention rules
Visibility to every account user
Use as an audience for a send
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sendable data extension can be selected as an audience when it is related to subscriber information.
whyWrong: Sendable status does not configure backups.
Retention policies can still apply.
Access is controlled by permissions and Business Unit scope.

sampleQuestions.question: Where can an administrator restrict the IP addresses allowed to sign in?
options: In each user’s role
In account security settings
In the Sender Authentication Package
In a delivery profile
sampleQuestions.explanation: Login IP restrictions are part of account security configuration.
whyWrong: Roles grant product permissions rather than limiting network addresses.
Sender authentication controls email delivery identity.
Delivery profiles configure sending behavior, not login access.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use folders and a consistent naming scheme for Marketing Cloud assets?
options: Find and safely update assets
Make journeys run faster
Improve deliverability automatically
Reduce storage charges
sampleQuestions.explanation: Clear organization helps teams identify assets and understand where changes may have an effect.
whyWrong: Folder structure does not change journey execution speed.
Folder names do not affect mailbox provider reputation.
Storage pricing is not reduced by naming conventions.
